note: Replies with the keyed answers both readers must find: `answers` is what the reader finds (typed_asks.keyed_answers, build_prototype.answered_keys, build_questionnaire.sent_answers, in test_keyed_replies.py), and `shell` what Firstmate's bin/fm-captain-ask.jq `reply` mode finds where it differs on purpose, with `why`. Invented text. Firstmate's own tests can read this file too.

cases.name: spaces around the equals sign and the value
a later answer to the same key wins
a value keeps its commas and equals signs
words between answers are not answers
a pointer line before the answers
cases.reply: Re your reply at 09:04 ("Which mapping"): Z1=a;Z2=b

cases.name: later is an answer for the reader and for Firstmate (the record keeps the card open)
only a capital letter and one or two digits is a key
a key with no value answers nothing
cases.why: Both readers drop an empty value. (build_questionnaire.sent_answers lists it with an empty value, and the reader's own code treats that as no answer.)

cases.name: the format's placeholder is not an answer for the reader
cases.why: Firstmate's reply reader keeps `...` as the value; the reader never takes it for an answer, so a placeholder that reaches a record is counted as the record's, not the captain's.

cases.name: an ellipsis character is a placeholder too
a long value is cut by Firstmate at 200 characters, not by the reader
cases.why: bin/fm-captain-ask.jq keeps the first 200 characters of a value; the reader shows what the captain typed.
